rubrics.intent_basis: Source and generated range mapping is repeatedly decomposed into document, map, and two offsets across feature callers.
rubrics.baseline_defect: The final patch makes callers repeatedly convert range endpoints to offsets and reconstruct positions, while the shared mapping boundary accepts only fragments.
rubrics.criterion: Source-range mapping used by feature providers is owned by a coherent boundary that accepts the related document, mapper, and range state together.
rubrics.acceptance: Equivalent APIs or local abstractions qualify when callers no longer repeat endpoint conversion and first mapped-range reconstruction for this path. A tuple, closure, associated records, encapsulated column storage, or complete existing mapping helper qualifies; no new class or exact return shape is required. One coherent projection operation may satisfy several consumer obligations. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Renaming getSourceRangeParts or wrapping its unchanged offset arguments at every call site.

rubrics.criterion: Generated-range mapping encapsulates the related source document, map, and range conversion for feature callers.
rubrics.acceptance: Code actions and color presentations can request mapped ranges without duplicating source endpoint conversion; all valid mapped ranges remain available where needed. A tuple, closure, associated records, encapsulated column storage, or complete existing mapping helper qualifies; no new class or exact return shape is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Keeping getGeneratedRangeParts with fragmented offsets and only shortening the call syntax.

rubrics.baseline_defect: The cache loop and updateRange each calculate line/character deltas, endpoint retention, and minimum nonempty range behavior.
rubrics.criterion: Diagnostic range updating has one coherent owner for both cached errors and direct updateRange use.
rubrics.acceptance: Both call paths share the mutation policy, including the endpoint rule, while keeping their own failure handling. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. rubrics.baseline_defect: transformTextEdit inspects start/end eligibility for ordinary, insert, and replace edits, while tryRecoverTextEdit receives disassembled positions and returns a tuple decoded by callers.
rubrics.criterion: Text-edit recovery owns the related range, replacement text, eligibility, and recovered result together for both ordinary and insert/replace edits.

Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. rubrics.intent_basis: Completion retry caching must keep each embedded document, provider, and result together as one entry through collection and incomplete-result refresh.
rubrics.baseline_defect: The expansion changes lastResult.results from records into parallel embeddedUris, plugins, and lists arrays; insertion and retry access rely on matching indexes, so the cache entry's related state has no cohesive owner.
rubrics.criterion: Maintain a coherent association between cached document identity, provider and completion result across seeding, refresh and combination.
rubrics.acceptance: Records, keyed association or encapsulated column storage qualify when updates cannot mismatch URI/plugin/list. Preserve list object references, null results, only incomplete refresh, captured old cache while awaiting, current plugin index lookup, initial versus refresh mapping filters, additional-service dedup and current lastResult combine behavior. No forced record-array representation. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Renaming the arrays, wrapping them together without changing index-coupled updates, or fixing only one push site.
